translationRepairs: After the usurper Zhu Youzhen seized power, Quan Yu was made military commissioner of Song.
After the commoner (Zhu Yougui) usurped the throne, Quan Yu was made military commissioner of Songzhou.

Focus 庶人篡位，授宋州節度使 names the usurper only as 庶人 and the post as 宋州節度使. In Later Liang usage 庶人 is Zhu Yougui (友珪) after degradation, not Zhu Youzhen; the prior idiomatic invents the wrong personal name and truncates 宋州 to Song. The proposed wording restores both points without new error.
(The 《Five Dynasties Essentials》 records that Quan Yu was posthumously honored as Minister of Works with the temple name Dejing.
(The 《Five Dynasties Essentials》 records that Quan Yu was posthumously honored as Director of the Imperial Secretariat with the posthumous title Dejing.

Focus 贈尚書令，諡德靖 grants Director of the Imperial Secretariat, not Minister of Works, and 諡 is a posthumous title, not a temple name. The revised replacement corrects both mistranslations without leaving untranslated Chinese in the English field.
Hu Zhu notes in the 《History of Liang》 biography of Prince Guang that Quan Yu was coarse and habitually addressed the emperor as "Third."
Your subject Hu notes in the 《History of Liang》 biography of Prince Guang that Quan Yu was coarse and habitually addressed the emperor as "Third."
Focus 臣護按 names the annotator only as 護 under the self-reference 臣; the prior idiomatic invents the surname Zhu. "Your subject Hu" restores 臣護 without changing the quoted biography content.
Pressing the rebel stronghold at Shilou, he charged from a ridge when Wang's line wavered; his horse fell and he died in the melee.
Pressing the rebel stronghold at Shilou, he charged from a ridge when the royal army slightly wavered; his horse fell and he died in the melee.
Focus 王師小卻 means the royal/imperial army slightly retreated; 王師 is not a person named Wang. The proposed wording corrects that misreading and preserves 小卻 as "slightly wavered."
